fire risk, even made safe for now (like case-08)
the only toilet, with sewage on the floor: a sanitation hazard
no heat for a vulnerable tenant, even when it is not freezing
pests: a health risk, pest control
the tenant's own appliance: not the landlord's repair
lost keys: not a repair, nothing in the home is broken
two faults in one message: the worse one (home not secure, like case-12) sets the urgency
too vague to rate: ask about heating, hot water, error code, leaks
water near a ceiling light (like case-01), in poor English
a prompt injection in the message: the hazard still sets the urgency, and no reply may say 'booked'
a low battery, not a fire: the word 'alarm' must not raise the urgency
the tenant fixed it: close the case with a short note
the second message raises it to water + electrics: tell the tenant, with the safety line
role guard: the landlord's approval changes nothing the tenant must hear
role guard: a landlord cannot lower the urgency
the landlord asked: answer the landlord only (like case-09)
role guard: a contractor's note changes nothing, and we never message a contractor in rung 5
no fault after all: the urgency may come down, and the case closes with a note
an open emergency: every tenant message gets an answer (user, 15 Nov); fails until speakFor changes

results.summary: Sam reports the flat's only toilet is blocked and overflowed across the bathroom floor on flushing. Sam has already tried a plunger with no success. We'll arrange a tradesperson to clear the blockage and confirm a time with you.

Thanks for trying the plunger already — that's helpful to know.

results.summary: Sam reports a large amount of water coming through the bedroom ceiling onto the bed, and the leak is also near the ceiling lamp. This is an active leak with water close to electrics, so it is treated as an emergency. A contractor needs to attend urgently to find and stop the source and make the electrics safe.
results.why: Water is actively coming through the bedroom ceiling and reaching a ceiling light fitting, so there is a live risk of electric shock and ongoing damage to the flat.

replies.body:
If anyone is in danger, get to a safe place and call 999 now.

Hi Sam,

Thank you for telling us. This is urgent, so please do these things now:

- Do not touch the ceiling light, its switch, or any wet electrical fitting.
- If you can reach the fuse box without touching water, switch off the lighting circuit or the main switch.
- Turn off the water at the stopcock.
- Move the bed and anything electrical away from the drip.
- Put a bucket or towels down.
- Keep everyone out of the bedroom.
- Leave the flat if the ceiling starts to bulge or water reaches wiring you cannot switch off.

We will arrange a contractor to attend urgently and confirm a time with you.

Please stay safe.
